key_insight: V-PaSS improves solar-cell prediction by representing mixed perovskite absorbers and device stacks in physically meaningful ways that let the model extrapolate to new alloys and unfamiliar architectures.
engineering_relevance: This gives perovskite design teams a more reliable screening tool for candidate materials and stack layouts that were not present in prior training data.
method: Interpolates mixed-cation, mixed-halide absorbers from 23 pure ABX3 endpoints using Vegard’s law plus learned bandgap bowing.
Encodes device structure with layer order, polarity (n-i-p or p-i-n), interfacial band offsets, and a scientific language model for chemical text.
Uses an institution-grouped evaluation so test devices come from unseen laboratories, stressing true extrapolation.
evidence_signal: Under unseen-laboratory testing, V-PaSS reached 2.861% MAE, outperforming a gradient-boosted baseline (3.017%) and the best tuned benchmark (2.912%), with especially large gains on unseen alloys and transport layers.
watch_item: Performance depends on having reliable endpoint crystal graphs, bandgap bowing estimates, and interfacial descriptors, so errors in these inputs could limit generalization to new chemistries.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
